sections.heading: Two research classes. One standard of relevance.
sections.body_html:
Industry-matched leads

Also called Look Alike leads: companies that match your agreed industries, territory and company criteria. An active or upcoming project is not required. Look Alike means a match to the written brief, not a prediction of buying intent.

Opportunity-signal leads

Relevant companies with an identified, evidenced project or development. The record explains what changed, why it may matter to your category and what remains unknown.

Target mix: we aim for 90% industry-matched leads and 10% opportunity-signal leads. This is not a guaranteed split. The final mix, counts and deliverables are agreed in writing. Both classes require fit checks and source traceability.

How our lead mix works

pages.h1: Account research for industrial suppliers selling into Ireland.
pages.intro_html:
Build a prospect base around the companies that fit your market—not only those with a newly announced project. Demand Range researches industry-matched accounts and adds project context where an evidenced signal is identified.

This is scoped, company-level research for suppliers of industrial equipment, technology and services, not a self-service contact database or a promise of meetings.

sections.heading: The targeting brief comes first.
sections.body_html:
Start with the product or service range and the applications you want to explore. Then agree:

  • Target industries, territory and relevant company characteristics.
  • Whether the research unit is a company or an individual facility.
  • The route to market: operators, OEMs, integrators or contractors, where relevant.
  • Existing accounts, channel conflicts and other exclusions.
  • The evidence needed to accept a record and the questions that can remain open.

Sector membership alone is not evidence of installed equipment, technical suitability or a current requirement.

sections.heading: What a company-level record contains.
sections.body_html:
The field set is agreed for the brief. A useful account record makes the following inspectable:

  • Identity: the company and, if in scope, the specific site.
  • Fit: industry, territory and the reason it matches the written criteria.
  • Evidence: source references and the relevant publication and review dates.
  • Class: industry-matched or opportunity-signal, with project research status kept separate.
  • Limits: exclusions, uncertainty and the next verification question.

Source access and customer-use permissions determine which evidence can accompany an output. A linked source is not, by itself, permission to redistribute its content.

See the editable example fields

sections.heading: Account fit does not require a project.
sections.body_html:
Industry-matched leads (Look Alike) meet the agreed profile without requiring an active or upcoming project. The record distinguishes a project search that was not required from a bounded review that found no qualifying signal. Neither means that no project exists.

Opportunity-signal leads meet the fit rules and have a relevant, evidenced project or development. Their brief separates the observed fact, commercial interpretation and unknowns.

We aim for 90% industry-matched and 10% opportunity-signal leads. This is a target, not a guaranteed mix. Exact counts, class treatment and deliverables are agreed in writing.

Neither decision establishes equipment suitability or demand. The written profile determines the fit decision.

sections.heading: Before you request a scope.
sections.body_html:
Are contacts included?

Not by default. This page describes company-level accounts. Named-person research and contact fields remain unagreed unless separately scoped and authorised with the required source, privacy and data controls. Outreach is a separate scope.

Can an account qualify without a project?

Yes. An industry-matched account can meet the written profile without a project signal. It is not automatically a marketing-qualified lead or a high-intent buyer.

Which territories can I request?

Ireland is the current focus. You can state other preferences in the quote request; coverage is assessed before any commitment.

How are deliverables agreed?

In writing: record unit, fields, sources, counts, class mix, timing, price and acceptance terms. A quote request does not book a package or guarantee coverage.

pages.meta_description: How Demand Range checks company fit, distinguishes project signals and records sources, review dates and unknowns. Inspect the method and fictional examples.
pages.h1: How the research classes and QA work
pages.intro_html:
Relevance comes first. A company must meet the written targeting criteria; a project signal is an additional evidence requirement for one class, not the definition of every lead.

Our method keeps company fit, observed evidence, interpretation and uncertainty separate. It does not infer private buying intent.

sections.heading: Start with a research unit and a written profile.
sections.body_html:
1. Define the brief. Agree the industries, territory, company criteria, exclusions and evidence requirements. Specify a company account or a facility record; do not count several sites as separate companies.
  2. Check source use. Identify sources that may be reviewed and what may be included in customer-facing output. Public access does not settle reuse rights.
  3. Resolve the entity. Check which company and site the evidence concerns; review parent/subsidiary relationships, duplicates and conflicts.
  4. Record the fit. Support each material criterion with a source reference and relevant dates. State why the account is included and what remains unresolved.
  5. Apply the class check. A project-signal record needs evidence of a relevant project or development as well as account fit.
  6. Review before release. Check the criteria, source posture and claims. A research pass is not, by itself, authority to deliver data or contact anyone.
provenance: SOP Required campaign decisions; Common acceptance; Independent QA; Delivery preparation

sections.heading: Two classes, with project research status kept separate.
sections.body_html:
Industry-matched leads (Look Alike)

A rules-based match to the agreed profile. No current or upcoming project is required. Where project research was not part of the brief, say not assessed—not required. Where an agreed bounded search found none, say no qualifying signal identified in the bounded review. Do not turn either statement into “no project exists”.

Opportunity-signal leads

A profile-matched account with a qualifying project or development signal supported by dated evidence. State the actual stage and the unknowns; do not infer an open tender, unawarded package or purchasing contact.

Both classes require source-supported fit. Our 90% industry-matched / 10% opportunity-signal mix is a target, not a guarantee. Counts and class treatment are agreed in writing. Neither class is automatically a marketing-qualified lead.

See both classes in a fictional example
provenance: SOP Canonical record classes; Class acceptance

sections.heading: Read the record in three layers.
sections.body_html:
Observed fact
What the source actually supports, attributed to that source and its date. An announcement of a proposed expansion is not evidence that construction or procurement has begun.
Interpretation
Why the fact may be relevant to the supplier’s range. An application hypothesis is not a verified technical match.
Unknown
Information not established: for example specifications, timing, procurement route or package availability. State the next useful check rather than filling the gap.

Keep publication dates distinct from retrieval or review dates. A recent review does not make an old source current. Reconcile conflicting sources before relying on a material claim.
provenance: BRAND Project context and visual evidence legend

sections.heading: A score cannot replace the fit decision.
sections.body_html:
The written criteria determine whether a record is accepted, held for review or rejected. Keep the decision reason visible. A score cannot rescue an excluded account or supply missing project evidence.

The detailed fictional opportunity brief includes an illustrative prioritisation score. It is not a buyer-intent score, a probability of sale or a quality ranking between the two lead classes.
provenance: BRAND §5 evidence legend and no class quality coding

Demand Range is an Irish industrial lead and account research business serving Ireland, the UK and the EU. pages.h1: Built for suppliers selling into industrial markets.
pages.intro_html:
Demand Range helps suppliers of industrial equipment, technology and services define and research relevant businesses. Ireland is the current focus; every brief needs its own territory, account criteria and exclusions.

A company can fit your market without a new project. Project and development signals add context where evidenced; they do not establish equipment demand.

sections.heading: Use the sector as a starting point, not the acceptance test.
sections.body_html:
These are scoping questions, not a claim of complete coverage or technical suitability.

Food and beverage

Which production businesses and activities belong in the brief? Distinguish manufacturers from distributors, retailers and hospitality businesses.

Pharma and life sciences

Which facility types and company activities matter to your range? State the technical requirements that need specialist confirmation.

Water, energy and utilities

Is the intended account an operator, an engineering business or a contractor? Keep account relevance separate from any project or procurement status.

Chemicals and process industries

Which process activities fit—and which applications or materials must be excluded or left for technical review?

Manufacturing and engineering

Do you sell to end users, machine builders or both? Set the company characteristics and site-level detail needed.

Construction and project delivery

Which contractors, integrators or engineering businesses are relevant routes? A project appointment alone does not establish control of an equipment package.
sections.baseline_anchor: Follow the change wherever it happens.

sections.heading: Specify the account route—not a promised contact.
sections.body_html:
• Operators: businesses operating the facilities or assets covered by the brief.
  • OEMs: manufacturers whose product or equipment scope may be relevant.
  • Integrators: businesses whose work may connect systems or equipment.
  • Contractors and engineering businesses: potential routes where their actual role is evidenced.

The same company can have more than one role. Confirm its activity and relationship to the relevant site or project rather than assuming purchasing authority. Role-level context is not a promise of named contacts, direct dials or buyer access.

A useful scope can exclude residential-only activity, irrelevant distribution models, territories outside your remit, existing accounts or channel conflicts. These are brief-specific choices, not universal judgments about those businesses.

pages.h1: What a supplier project-intelligence brief includes
pages.intro_html:
When an evidenced industrial project or development is relevant to your range, the useful question is what it actually establishes. Demand Range’s Opportunity Intelligence capability brings the source record, supplier relevance and unresolved questions into a reviewable brief.

It supports the opportunity-signal component of our wider account-research model. Not every industry-matched account needs a project.

sections.heading: What the brief needs to make clear.
sections.body_html:
• Company and facility: which entity the source refers to and how it relates to the target account.
  • Observed change: the specific project or development, with source references and dates.
  • Supplier relevance: why the change may matter to the agreed product or service category.
  • Stage and route: what is known about progress and the organisations involved; what is not established.
  • Unknowns and review: specification gaps, package status, timing and the next verification step.

Outputs, evidence supplied and review cadence are agreed for the brief. This is not a continuous live feed or a promise of complete project coverage. Role-level mapping does not include named contacts by default.

sections.heading: A signal is not an open equipment order.
sections.body_html:
Observed

State exactly what the source supports. For example, a fictional company statement proposes additional production space.

Inferred

The change may be worth reviewing against the supplier’s range. That is a relevance hypothesis—not proof of required equipment.

Unknown

Whether the project will proceed, which specifications apply, how procurement will run and whether any package is available.

This example is invented to explain the method. In real work, planning, construction, tender and award evidence must keep their actual meanings and dates. An award notice cannot support a claim that the same work remains unawarded.

pages.intro_html:
See the difference between evidence and a qualified account. The first section uses three real EPA dataset records to show literal source fields, research decisions and remaining checks. It is a facility-evidence demonstration, not a finished prospect list or client result.

The later targeting brief, accepted/rejected accounts, project-signal example and downloadable example rows are fictional teaching material. No personal contacts are included. Neither section demonstrates the 90/10 target proportions or authorises outreach.

sections.heading: The fictional targeting brief
sections.body_html:
Example profile DEMO-PROFILE-01: an industrial process-equipment supplier wants to research food-and-beverage manufacturing companies operating production facilities in Ireland. The record unit is the company. Existing accounts and known channel conflicts would be excluded in a real brief; this invented exercise contains none.

Exclude residential-only retailers and businesses without relevant manufacturing activity. An active project is not required for the industry-matched class. For this exercise, the opportunity-signal class requires a source statement identifying a proposed facility expansion at a relevant manufacturing company.

This brief tests account relevance only. It does not assess installed equipment, hygienic requirements, technical compatibility, purchasing authority or buying timing.
provenance: Editorial: fictional demonstration profile, not a client requirement

sections.heading: Accepted for account fit: Fictional Beverage Manufacturer A
sections.body_html:
Fictional example · DEMO-ACCOUNT-A · Accepted within this illustration only.

Company and territory
Fictional Beverage Manufacturer A; beverage manufacturing; Ireland; company-level record.
Invented source statement
DEMO-SOURCE-A: an invented company activity statement says the business operates a beverage-production facility in Ireland. No live source was retrieved.
Fit reason
The stipulated activity and location meet the example profile’s manufacturing and territory rules.
Research class
Industry-matched lead (Look Alike): fit_matched_lookalike.
Project research status
Not assessed—not required: not_assessed_not_required. This is not a finding that no project exists.
Unknowns
Installed equipment, specifications, current needs and purchasing route are not established.
Next check
In real work, verify company identity and source-supported fit, assess source-use rights and complete duplicate/conflict checks before an acceptance decision.

Why include it? The written account criteria are met in the fictional scenario. No project or buyer-intent claim is needed to explain that fit.
provenance: Editorial: original synthetic record, no real evidence or QA pass

sections.heading: Paired signal example: Fictional Beverage Manufacturer B
sections.body_html:
Fictional example · DEMO-SIGNAL-B · Accepted within this illustration only.

Company and territory
Fictional Beverage Manufacturer B; beverage manufacturing; Ireland; company-level record.
Invented source statements
DEMO-SOURCE-B-FIT describes an Irish beverage-production business. DEMO-SOURCE-B-PROJECT says it proposes adding production space at its facility. Both statements are invented; no planning record or company announcement was retrieved.
Observed fact within the fiction
A proposed facility expansion is described. Construction, procurement and equipment selection are not established.
Fit and signal decision
The company meets the same account profile, and the stipulated expansion meets this example’s signal definition.
Research class and status
Opportunity-signal lead: opportunity_signal; qualifying signal identified: qualifying_signal_identified—within the invented scenario only.
Interpretation
The proposed change gives a reason to investigate relevance to the supplier’s range. It does not establish a requirement for a particular product.
Unknowns and next check
Confirm actual stage, specifications and procurement route in real work. Package availability, buyer access and intent remain unknown. No outreach is authorised by the example.

What changed? There is an additional project-evidence requirement, not a higher guarantee of quality or conversion. A real signal record would also need dates, current evidence, rights checks and independent QA.

sections.heading: Rejected for fit: Fictional Home Pump Retailer C
sections.body_html:
Fictional example · DEMO-REJECT-C · Rejected within this illustration.

Company and territory
Fictional Home Pump Retailer C; residential equipment retail; Ireland; company-level candidate.
Invented source statement
DEMO-SOURCE-C says the business sells domestic pumps to householders and does not conduct food-or-beverage manufacturing. This is an invented positive description, not an inference from missing information.
Tested class
Candidate assessed for fit_matched_lookalike; not accepted or counted as a delivered lead.
Project research status
not_assessed_not_required.
Failed criterion
DEMO-PROFILE-01 requires relevant manufacturing activity and excludes residential-only retailers.
Decision reason
Business-type mismatch. A shared product word—“pump”—does not override the targeting brief.
Next step
Exclude from this example scope. Do not invent a project or soften the criterion to make the candidate fit.

This is a rejection against one brief, not a claim that the business would be unsuitable for every supplier.

sections.heading: Edit the fields without treating the sample as live data.
sections.body_html:
The blank worksheet and small field dictionary are available without registration. They are an educational starting point for discussing company-level research, not the full internal QA schema or an agreed delivery specification.

  • Blank account worksheet (CSV)
  • Editable field dictionary (CSV)
  • Fictional worked rows (CSV)

The fields keep identity, profile, source references, dates, class, project status, interpretation, unknowns and decision separate. Dates are blank in the fictional rows because no source was published or reviewed. Demonstration source IDs are not live citations.

A real record needs permitted sources, current identity and fit evidence, applicable data controls and the agreed review/release checks. Downloading or completing a worksheet does not clear source rights or authorise outreach.

sections.heading: Apply the same questions to your market.
sections.body_html:
What must a company do, where must it operate, what should be excluded and what evidence would justify inclusion? Define those answers before deciding how many accounts to research.

decisions: MAP C03 supplies the actual proposed title/H1. The brief and companies are deliberately generic fictional labels rather than real firms or realistic contact identities.

Two accepted illustrative records demonstrate both classes; a third record demonstrates a concrete rejection. This is not a 90/10 batch, simulated client delivery or execution of the separately tracked synthetic rehearsal.
All source statements are visibly invented; no fabricated URLs, retrieval dates, official records or live research receipts. No outside facts require public citations.
The CSV dictionary is a public educational subset. Canonical internal class/state identifiers are preserved exactly; public decision labels are not independent QA approval.
pages.risks: Keep a fiction label on every example and every exported example row. Do not restyle accepted/rejected as hot/cold or make the signal class higher quality. Do not strip the source/date and rights caveats during integration. No real-company or customer-use rights have been cleared by writing these examples.
